verdict.rationale: Ghostty's docs say it renders ligature fonts correctly and lets users enable or disable specific font features (e.g. `-calt` for programming ligatures). A repeatable font config specifies preferred fallback fonts, and there are further knobs such as synthetic-style control and an embedded JetBrains Mono with built-in nerd fonts. One user reported blurrier font rendering than xfce4-terminal, which lowers confidence in rendering quality but does not contradict these capabilities. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained metric tuning beyond font features and synthetic styles (e.g. size, cell or line-height adjustments), and independent hands-on corroboration of ligature and fallback behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use programming fonts with ligatures, fallback fonts, and fine-grained font tuning

citations.quote: You can use fonts that have ligatures and Ghostty will render them correctly. You can also specify specific font features to enable or disable.
To disable programming ligatures, use `-calt` since this is the typical feature name for programming ligatures.
This configuration can be repeated multiple times to specify preferred fallback fonts when the requested codepoint is not available in the primary font.
Set this to "false" or "true" to disable or enable synthetic styles completely.
